Build a recurring decision briefing

Source: vignettes/daily-briefing.Rmd
daily-briefing.Rmd

A useful daily or weekly briefing is an attention system. It answers four questions without manufacturing novelty:

  1. What changed? Verified claims that do not restate what the team already accepted.
  2. Why does it matter? Labeled, confidence-calibrated assessments bound to their supporting claims.
  3. What needs review today? Concrete proposed actions, clearly distinct from established facts.
  4. What held steady? Explicit no-change signals—emitted only when today’s verified evidence actually reconfirms an accepted claim (never when evidence is missing or inconclusive).

You do not need a separate briefing framework. Your host script owns the schedule and approval policy, Tempest runs the research and computes the change signal structurally against pinned accepted claims, Graft stores exact selections and human review decisions, and scans audits completed trajectories.

1. Load your accepted briefing basis

Start by opening your Graft store and checking whether a previous accepted checkpoint exists. On day one, knowledge is NULL and every verified claim is new. On later runs, reuse the exact previously accepted decision after verifying current eligibility:

library(tempest)
library(graft)
source(system.file("examples", "briefing-basis.R", package = "tempest"))

store <- graft_store("briefing/memory", create = TRUE)
basis_path <- "briefing/basis.rds"
knowledge <- NULL

if (file.exists(basis_path)) {
  basis <- readRDS(basis_path)
  # Inspect any decisions recorded since the last run
  changes <- briefing_changes(store, basis)
  knowledge <- reuse_briefing_basis(
    store,
    basis,
    eligible = function(event) host_allows(event)
  )
}

If another reviewer corrected or withdrew the stream in the meantime, reuse_briefing_basis() stops rather than silently substituting a different basis—giving your host a chance to inspect changes first.

2. Run today’s briefing

Pass knowledge into tempest_run(). Use a focused expert panel matched to the decision at hand:

experts <- list(
  tempest_expert(
    name = "Technical reviewer",
    title = "Process and scale-up specialist",
    description = "Evaluates demonstrated operating performance and technical risk.",
    instructions = "Separate measured plant results from projections.",
    focus_areas = c("yield", "scale-up", "safety")
  ),
  tempest_expert(
    name = "Market and policy reviewer",
    title = "Supply-chain and regulatory analyst",
    description = "Tracks policy changes, capacity expansions, and economics.",
    instructions = "Distinguish binding rules and operating plants from announcements.",
    focus_areas = c("policy", "capacity", "economics")
  )
)

result <- tempest_run(
  paste(
    "Decision briefing on grid-scale battery recycling as of", Sys.Date(),
    "highlighting what changed, why it matters, what needs review,",
    "and any material no-change signal backed by verified evidence."
  ),
  config = tempest_config(
    models = "openai/gpt-5.6-luna",
    citation_policy = "claim_verified",
    on_unsupported_claim = "flag"
  ),
  knowledge = knowledge,
  experts = experts,
  max_questions_per_perspective = 2,
  output_dir = "briefing/runs",
  run_id = paste0("briefing-", Sys.Date())
)

report <- tempest_report(result)
claims <- tempest_claims(result)
supports <- tempest_claim_supports(result)

Tempest decides structurally—not just via prompts—whether each verified claim belongs under What changed or No material change by comparing it against active Claim records in knowledge.

3. Publish, review, and accept deliberately

Publish today’s run as a candidate selection in Graft and inspect its trajectory before deciding whether to advance the accepted briefing stream:

selection <- tempest_publish_artifact_research(result, store)
review <- tempest_trajectory_review(result)

# On an unchanged day, keep the briefing report in your run log without
# manufacturing a new accepted knowledge revision.
# When a reviewer confirms a real update or correction, advance the stream:
previous <- if (file.exists(basis_path)) basis$decision else NULL

accepted <- graft_accept(
  store,
  graft_read_selection(store, selection),
  stream = "battery-briefing",
  expected = previous,
  key = paste0("review-", Sys.Date()),
  actor = "briefing-reviewer",
  reason = "Reviewed today's new claims and source spans",
  purpose = "briefing"
)

basis <- capture_briefing_basis(store, "battery-briefing", accepted@id, "briefing")
saveRDS(basis, basis_path)

Because expected = previous is explicit, two reviewers cannot silently overwrite each other’s decisions. If evidence later turns out to be flawed, record a withdrawal—future runs stop consulting that stream while historical briefings remain readable:

graft_withdraw(
  store,
  stream = "battery-briefing",
  expected = basis$decision,
  key = paste0("withdraw-", Sys.Date()),
  actor = "briefing-reviewer",
  reason = "Primary source retracted; re-evaluate next cycle"
)

# Historical inspection remains available even after withdrawal
historical <- read_briefing_basis(store, basis)

4. Pair with interactive review and scans

You can open any briefing run inside tempest_mcp_app(result) for read-only claim inspection, serve your accepted "battery-briefing" stream to chat agents with graft::graft_tools(), or project tempest_trajectory_review() into scans to monitor run reliability over time. See Research that remembers with Graft for the full composition guide.
